facts: Magnetic force on a moving charge depends on charge, velocity, magnetic field, and the angle between velocity and field.
The magnetic force is perpendicular to both the velocity and the magnetic field.
A charge moving parallel to a magnetic field experiences no magnetic force.

keyTerms.df: Magnetic force is the interaction on a moving charge that varies with charge, velocity, magnetic field, and the angle between velocity and field.
keyTerms.eg: A charge crossing a magnetic field can have a magnetic force that changes when its velocity direction changes.
keyTerms.mi: Magnetic force points along the velocity of the charge.
keyTerms.cx: The force is not along the velocity; it is perpendicular to both the velocity and the magnetic field.

keyTerms.df: A moving charge is a charged object with velocity, so its magnetic force depends on that velocity and its direction relative to the magnetic field.
keyTerms.eg: A moving charge with velocity parallel to the field is a case with no magnetic force.
keyTerms.mi: Any charge must feel magnetic force whether it is moving or not.
keyTerms.cx: The dependence is on a moving charge, so the velocity and its angle to the field matter.

keyTerms.df: A magnetic field is the field in this relation that sets the direction and orientation used to determine the magnetic force on a moving charge.
keyTerms.eg: A magnetic field compared with a charge's velocity helps determine whether the force is present and how it is oriented.
keyTerms.mi: A magnetic field can only be compared by its strength, not by its direction.
keyTerms.cx: Direction matters because the force depends on the angle between velocity and field and is perpendicular to both.

scenario.su: A student records a charge moving through a magnetic field and needs to decide whether the magnetic force is present. The lab note says the velocity is parallel to the magnetic field, and the setup must be judged before the next run.
scenario.ma: Notebook entry: velocity parallel to magnetic field; diagram sketch: arrows drawn in the same direction; observation log: no magnetic force marker; comparison card: a perpendicular setup shown beside the parallel setup.

mc.q: A diagram records a moving charge with labeled velocity and magnetic-field arrows. To complete the diagram, which force-arrow relationship should a student choose?
op: Perpendicular to both velocity and magnetic-field arrows
Along velocity and perpendicular to magnetic-field arrow
Perpendicular to velocity and along magnetic-field arrow
Along both velocity and magnetic-field arrows
mc.ex: The magnetic force is perpendicular to both the velocity and the magnetic field, which matches a force arrow perpendicular to both recorded arrows. The choice combining alignment with velocity and perpendicularity to the field conflicts with the required perpendicular relationship to velocity.

mc.q: A test-run record says a charge moves parallel to the magnetic-field arrow. Which interpretation should the student choose when labeling the magnetic-force observation?
op: Experiences force in its velocity direction
Experiences force perpendicular to its velocity
Experiences force opposite its velocity direction
mc.ex: Because the charge moves parallel to the magnetic field, it experiences no magnetic force, which matches the no-force interpretation. The perpendicular-to-velocity choice incorrectly applies a force direction to this parallel-motion case, where no magnetic force is experienced.
